sections.heading: Devnet 8 and Devnet 11 Status
sections.summary: Devnet 8 is stabilized with clients back to head; two Besu-related scenarios remain to be rerun; devnet 11 testing is finalized and will be torn down.
sections.body:
- Devnet 8 has been re-stabilized; all clients are back to head.
  - Two open scenarios still affect Besu: a JUMP test issue and an attack scenario launched earlier in the week.
  - Both scenarios are prepared and will be rerun today or tomorrow.
- Devnet 11 testing is finalized; Optimism and Lido confirmed no remaining findings, so the network will be shut down today.
- Primary testing should continue on devnet 8.
- Relays/builders: no update on Titan or ultrasound relays; Potuz confirmed bids are being received but not heavily tested due to early bugs.

sections.heading: CL Block-Serving Window After EIP-8061
sections.summary: No decision was reached; the serving window question will continue async and be brought to ACDE, as it is a governance decision affecting both layers.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8061](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8061) reduces the weak subjectivity period (WSP), but the CL block-serving window (`compute_min_epochs_for_block_requests()`) stayed at 33024 epochs (~5 months).
- Three options presented: keep 33024, reduce to ~14299 (same derivation under EIP-8061), or reduce to 8192 ([EIP-8383](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12188), PFI for Hegota).
- Reducing from 33K to ~14K would save roughly 144 GB of BAL storage on the EL side.
- Potuz argued the CL database has never been a size concern and that this is a governance decision for ACD, not ACDT.
- Toni noted this ties into a broader effort to unify retention windows across EL clients (including state diffs); agreed to bring the BAL retention question to the next ACDE.
- Nico Flaig pointed out that EL retention drives CL storage strategy: if ELs prune BALs, CLs cannot dedupe payloads and must store them in full.
  - EL clients behave differently: Geth retains BALs for the full period; others prune at ~3533 epochs.
  - Lodestar only dedupes finalized data; Teku and Prysm blind everything as soon as it hits storage, including non-finalized payloads.
- Potuz argued that for re-execution/state regeneration, the network is broken long before 33K epochs of non-finality, so the retention serves mainly history availability.
- Nico countered that even in the happy case (node offline for 2 months), the EL needs BALs to sync back to head without checkpoint sync.
- Potuz maintained that checkpoint sync plus backfill provides equivalent assurances if the chain is finalizing.
- Kevaundray proposed continuing the discussion async via a Discord thread, linking to [this thread](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1549841282652971111).
- Agreement: Toni will bring the BAL retention topic to the next ACDE.

sections.heading: BAL Retention Period Alignment (EIP-7928)
sections.summary: BAL retention should match the CL serving window to enable deduplication; Toni volunteered to bring the topic to the next ACDE for EL client input.
sections.body:
- Cayman noted that BAL retention should match the CL retention window, or deduping payloads becomes unreliable.
- [EIP-7928 PR](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12347) proposes aligning BAL retention from 3533 to 33024 epochs.
- Lighthouse, Teku, Prysm, and Lodestar all blind BALs or plan to, rebuilding payloads from the EL.
- Toni confirmed goal should be enabling safe deduplication of BALs by CL clients.
- Marius confirmed Geth uses BALs for snap sync healing but acknowledged even during non-finality this is not a problem since pivots are fresh.
- No EL client representatives from Nethermind or others spoke to the topic on-call.
- Decision deferred to ACDE, with Toni volunteering to bring it up.

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Testnet Schedule
sections.summary: Sepolia fork confirmed for October 6 (epoch 353024); client releases due September 29; Hoodi tentatively October 27 with go/no-go October 8; Sepolia shadow fork to be scheduled this week.
sections.body:
- Sepolia Glamsterdam activation confirmed for October 6, epoch 353024, 13:53:36 UTC.
  - PR to review: [ethclients/sepolia#126](https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/126).
  - Related PRs: [pm#2205](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/2205), [EIPs#12355](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12355).
- Client releases are due September 29.
- Hoodi tentatively scheduled for October 27, with a go/no-go decision on October 8.
- Sepolia shadow fork not yet scheduled; PK noted they were waiting for Lighthouse last week but plan to schedule it this week.
- The CL retention window question is not considered a blocker for testnet deployment.
  - Toni and Parithosh both confirmed it should not block testnets; it is an optimization.
- Stable Amsterdam test fixtures (execution-specs `v21.0.0`) aim to be released Wednesday, bumping the major version to match client main branches moving Amsterdam code.
  - Relevant tracking issue: [execution-specs#3217](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/issues/3217).

sections.heading: Preliminary Hegota Devnet Schedule
sections.summary: Agreement to start with separate FOCIL-only and Frames-only devnets, then combine later; a Frames devnet-0 is targeted soon, with a combined FOCIL+Frames devnet before DevCon.
sections.body:
- Spencer proposed aligning on a loose Hegota devnet plan early to avoid repeating Glamsterdam's mistake of underestimating complex EIPs (e.g., EIP-8037).
  - Goal: include more complex EIPs earlier in the devnet cycle and potentially reduce total number of devnets.
- Stefan (EthPandaOps) favored separating EL-only (Frames, [EIP-8141](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8141)) and CL-only ([FOCIL](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7805)) devnets initially, then combining into a Hegota devnet once basics are stable.
- Toni noted that unlike ePBS and BALs (which had ~zero interaction), FOCIL and Frames have significant EL-side interaction, especially around the mempool and building inclusion lists with frame transactions.
- Potuz agreed but noted the CL-side interaction of FOCIL with frames/AA is trivial; CL-only FOCIL devnet can proceed independently.
- lightclient proposed: Frames devnet-0 first; if it goes well, target a combined FOCIL+Frames devnet in October, ideally working before DevCon.
  - Some spec items for Frames are still pending for subsequent devnets.
- Jihoon noted that even a FOCIL-only devnet requires minor EL changes (EL must produce inclusion lists), and a Frames+FOCIL EL devnet needs minor CL modifications.
  - Suggested sequence: FOCIL-only and Frames-only first → stabilize → modify CL for combined EL testing → full Hegota devnet-0.
- Iván (ethrex) noted 3 EL clients already have frame transaction implementations, while FOCIL still has only 2 CLs trying to agree.
- Frames test releases already exist: [execution-specs releases](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases).
- PSA at the end of the shared section (no decision taken on this call): [EIP-8142](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8142) (Block-in-Blobs) is being withdrawn by its champion, who has proposed [EIP-8411](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12299) (Fast Execution Payload Broadcast) as a replacement — see the [withdrawal comment](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12072#issuecomment-5757125260).
  - CL teams were asked to add ratings for EIP-8411 ahead of the next ACDC.

sections.heading: BPO Test Schedules for Amsterdam
sections.summary: Existing Osaka-based BPO3/BPO4 test schedules will be kept until the fork; new Amsterdam-based schedules will be added with descriptive names like BPOIncrease/BPODecrease.
sections.body:
- Current test fixtures include BPO transitions based on Osaka (BPO2 → BPO3 increase, BPO2 → BPO4 decrease).
- Plan: keep Osaka-based BPO3/BPO4 until after the Amsterdam fork; add new Amsterdam-based BPO test schedules.
- Proposed naming for new schedules: `BPOIncrease` and `BPODecrease` (decoupled from numbered fork names) rather than BPO5/BPO6.
- No EL client objections raised on the call; danceratopz will create a PR to propose the naming.
- Stefan noted blobs are not hitting limits currently, so blob count increases are not urgent.
- Running new BPO schedules in hive requires clients to accept a BPO slot after Amsterdam.

sections.heading: Benchmarking Hardware Targets
sections.summary: Ben Adams raised whether benchmarking should target attester-node hardware (double spec) instead of full-node hardware; discussion deferred to tomorrow's gaslighting committee call.
sections.body:
- Current benchmarking targets the EIP-7870 minimum full-node spec (weaker hardware).
- Ben Adams proposed also testing attester-node hardware (roughly double), since attesters have stricter deadlines (must meet worst-case within a shorter window) while full nodes can average out.
- Toni noted that with ePBS, attesters no longer need to execute the payload before attesting — only by the next slot.
- Maria Silva argued benchmarking should still target low-powered nodes to properly price opcodes for network-wide DOS protection, not just attester performance.
- Łukasz Rozmej noted the distinction: worst-case (DOS) scenarios should use attester spec; average-case (10x lighter) is what full nodes actually process.
- Ben will bring the topic to tomorrow's dedicated gaslighting committee call for further discussion.
  - Tracking issue: [gas-lighting-tracker#83](https://github.com/ethpandaops/gas-lighting-tracker/issues/83).
